mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved monotonically for four consecutive weeks (-19.0 to -17.7). This momentum reflects an underlying recovery trend in discretionary mobility that is expected to persist, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose each of the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days despite the prior 4-week monotonic rise.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 3.4 points in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks following a PARKS jump greater than 3 points in a given week.

The joint stabilization of commuting-related mobility signals a resumption of routine weekday activity patterns that jointly drive incidental retail visits, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES variance across weeks stays within 2 points while TRANSIT improves by more than 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 4 weeks even though both WORKPLACES remains stable and TRANSIT continues to improve.

evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 15.3 to 14.6 over 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 2 weeks despite continued week-on-week decline in RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained positive and stable (around +1.3 to +2.3) for three consecutive weeks, indicating no new restrictions are suppressing essential retail access. This policy stability signals an absence of tightening measures, allowing broader RETAIL_REC recovery to continue over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 0 for at least 3 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 4 weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM staying positive throughout, indicating policy stability does not translate to retail gains.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp rise in PARKS mobility reflects a seasonal shift toward favorable outdoor weather, which substitutes leisure time away from indoor retail and recreation venues, causing RETAIL_REC growth to decelerate or reverse over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 3 points in two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose sharply in the latest week after two weeks of decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 2 weeks even as PARKS mobility keeps climbing, falsifying the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed near -28 to -30 while RETAIL_REC has been recovering, suggesting people are substituting car or local walking trips for public transit to reach retail destinations. This decoupling should sustain short-term RETAIL_REC gains even without transit recovery.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -25 while RETAIL_REC improves by more than 1 point week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed near -28 to -30 while RETAIL_REC rose each week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next week while TRANSIT remains below -25, indicating no decoupling effect.

candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 2 points while WORKPLACES changes less than 1 point in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 3.4 points while WORKPLACES changed only 0.3 points in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks despite simultaneous PARKS growth and WORKPLACES stagnation, falsifying the rebalancing mechanism.
